newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST-Trelleborg Q1 profit seen falling 34 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Trelleborg Q1 profit seen falling 34 pct.

text.p: Swedish metals and rubber group Trelleborg was expected to post a 34 percent fall in first quarter pre-tax profit to 317 million crowns, according to a Reuter poll of nine analysts on Wednesday.
Forecasts ranged from 260 million crowns to 405 million.
In the corresponding quarter last year, the profit amounted to 478 million crowns.
For the full-year 1997, analysts expected a profit of 1.47 billion crowns and for 1998, the profit was seen at 1.66 billion crowns.
Analysts said the wide span in forecasts could stem from different calculations on Trelleborg's numerous acquisitions and on the effect of currency hedging after the dollar has strengthened.
The average forecast for 1997 has been raised by 26 percent since Reuters survey ahead of the company's annual report. Metal prices and, above all, the dollar, has also strengthened since.
Trelleborg will release first quarter earnings on April 25.
Analysts interviewed were from Aros, Carnegie, Den Norske Bank, Den Danske Bank, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Hagstromer & Qviberg, Handelsbanken, Penser and Swedbank
